purpose: Evaluate faithful capture of statements in fictional primary-care follow-up conversations. This is not a clinical accuracy or safety benchmark.

cases.name: Routine follow-up with symptom and history

segments.speaker: Patient
segments.text: I'm here for my usual diabetes follow-up.

segments.speaker: Patient
segments.text: I've had dry mouth for two days.

segments.speaker: Clinician
segments.text: We'll meet again in three months.

gold_facts.quote: I'm here for my usual diabetes follow-up.
gold_facts.speaker: Patient
gold_facts.normalized_statement: The patient says this is their usual diabetes follow-up.

gold_facts.quote: I've had dry mouth for two days.
gold_facts.speaker: Patient
gold_facts.normalized_statement: The patient reports dry mouth.

gold_facts.quote: I've had dry mouth for two days.
gold_facts.speaker: Patient
gold_facts.normalized_statement: The dry mouth has lasted two days.

gold_facts.quote: We'll meet again in three months.
gold_facts.speaker: Clinician
gold_facts.normalized_statement: The clinician says they will meet again in three months.

must_not_infer: A blood glucose value or trend
A diagnosis beyond the patient's stated diabetes follow-up
cases.why_useful: Checks a direct symptom, its duration, a stated ongoing-care context, and a spoken follow-up interval.

cases.name: Explicit symptom denial

segments.speaker: Patient
segments.text: I haven't felt dizzy this week.

segments.speaker: Patient
segments.text: My appetite has been lower since Monday.

segments.speaker: Clinician
segments.text: I have not made an assessment today.

segments.speaker: Patient
segments.text: I'm here for my regular diabetes follow-up.

gold_facts.speaker: Patient
gold_facts.normalized_statement: The patient denies dizziness this week.

gold_facts.quote: I haven't felt dizzy this week.
gold_facts.speaker: Patient
gold_facts.normalized_statement: The patient describes the timeframe of the dizziness denial as this week.

gold_facts.quote: My appetite has been lower since Monday.
gold_facts.speaker: Patient
gold_facts.normalized_statement: The patient reports lower appetite.

gold_facts.quote: My appetite has been lower since Monday.
gold_facts.speaker: Patient
gold_facts.normalized_statement: The lower appetite has been present since Monday.

gold_facts.quote: I have not made an assessment today.
gold_facts.speaker: Clinician
gold_facts.normalized_statement: The clinician says no assessment was made today.

gold_facts.quote: I'm here for my regular diabetes follow-up.
gold_facts.speaker: Patient
gold_facts.normalized_statement: The patient says they are here for a regular diabetes follow-up.

must_not_infer: The patient has no other symptoms
A cause for the appetite change
cases.why_useful: Tests whether a clear negation remains a denial while nearby positive symptom statements are captured separately.

cases.name: Patient corrects an earlier duration

segments.speaker: Patient
segments.text: The tingling began four days ago.

segments.speaker: Patient
segments.text: Correction: it began yesterday, not four days ago.

segments.speaker: Patient
segments.text: I still attend my regular diabetes visits.

gold_facts.quote: Correction: it began yesterday, not four days ago.
gold_facts.speaker: Patient
gold_facts.normalized_statement: The patient corrects the onset to yesterday; it did not begin four days ago.

gold_facts.quote: I still attend my regular diabetes visits.
gold_facts.speaker: Patient
gold_facts.normalized_statement: The patient says they continue attending regular diabetes visits.

must_not_infer: A change to the patient's ongoing care
cases.why_useful: Checks that the corrected duration replaces the earlier value without losing the explicit negation of the old value.

cases.name: Uncertain medication name and dose

segments.speaker: Patient
segments.text: I take a small white tablet, maybe five milligrams.

segments.speaker: Patient
segments.text: I don't know its name.

segments.speaker: Clinician

segments.speaker: Patient
segments.text: This is my usual diabetes follow-up.

gold_facts.quote: I take a small white tablet, maybe five milligrams.
gold_facts.speaker: Patient
gold_facts.normalized_statement: The patient reports taking a small white tablet; the dose may be five milligrams.

gold_facts.quote: I don't know its name.
gold_facts.speaker: Patient
gold_facts.normalized_statement: The patient does not know the tablet's name.

gold_facts.quote: Please bring the package next time.
gold_facts.speaker: Clinician

expected_review_prompts: Clarify the tablet name and confirm whether the patient-recalled dose is five milligrams.
cases.why_useful: Tests preservation of incomplete medication details and their uncertainty without filling in a plausible drug or schedule.

cases.name: Ambiguous speaker and medication statement

segments.speaker: Patient
segments.text: This is a routine follow-up for my ongoing asthma care.

gold_facts.quote: Maybe it was two tablets; I can't remember who changed it.
gold_facts.speaker: Unknown

gold_facts.speaker: Patient

gold_facts.quote: The medication details remain unclear in this conversation.
gold_facts.speaker: Clinician

expected_review_prompts: Clarify which medication is being discussed, the amount, who made the change, and when it happened.
cases.why_useful: Combines unknown speaker attribution with explicitly uncertain medication amount, actor, and timing.
